instrument: Fort Laramie (Horse Creek), Sept. 17, 1851 (Kappler II 594; 11 Stat. 749 stub)

revision_note: 2026-10-20: was contested; the contested case is the 426 split north and west of the South Platte (426-N), per K1 s.4.2. 399 is the 1851 Blackfoot territory, made a common hunting ground in 1855, with no cession of its own.

instrument: Fort Wise, Feb. 18, 1861 (12 Stat. 1163); Little Arkansas, Oct. 14, 1865 (14 Stat. 703); recognized by Fort Laramie 1851
basis: Ten Southern chiefs signed in 1861 (no Northern Cheyenne or Northern Arapaho, Council of 44 had refused); Little Arkansas relinquishment 10.5 months after Sand Creek by a minority; ICC Dockets 329/348 valued 51.21M acres at $23.5M as of Oct. 14, 1865 (about 46 cents an acre). Not flagged senate_amended_no_consent: an Oct. 29, 1861 assent paper exists (TREC disputes its marks). 100,000 gold-rush trespassers 1858-61.

instrument: Fort Wise 1861 (12 Stat. 1163); Little Arkansas 1865 (14 Stat. 703) Art. 2; Fort Laramie with Northern Cheyenne and Northern Arapaho, May 10, 1868 (15 Stat. 655) Art. 2
basis: VERIFY OVERRIDE: not 'never ceded'. Ceded on paper (1861, 1865, 1868), contested by the Northern Cheyenne and Northern Arapaho and by 1862-63 federal officials (Commissioner's 1862 report 'imperfect and indefinite'; U.S. Attorney Browne 1863). Attribute 'never validly ceded' to the Northern nations and TREC.

instrument: None (Spanish Fork treaty of June 1865 unratified but enforced)
basis: Royce p. 824: 'taken possession of by U. S. without formal purchase'. PSL p. 369: Army enforced the unratified 1865 treaty and removed Utes from the Wasatch Front.

instrument: Act of Feb. 21, 1863
basis: Ho-Chunk Blue Earth reserve sold by statute in the post-1862 wave although the Ho-Chunk were not party to the war.

instrument: Acts of Feb. 16, 1863 (12 Stat. 652) and Mar. 3, 1863 (12 Stat. 819)
basis: Crosswalk says ceded 1863-03-03, but no cession: Congress annulled the Dakota treaties and ordered the reserve sold while about 1,600 non-combatants were interned at Fort Snelling (130-300 died) after the Mankato mass execution. 'massacre_linked' here covers mass execution and internment, not a massacre in the strict sense.

instrument: Nez Perce treaty, June 9, 1863 (14 Stat. 647)
basis: Signed by Lawyer's faction after non-treaty bands left; cut the 1855 reserve about 90 percent and ceded homelands of bands that never signed (Wallowa). Big Hole (1877) killed 60-90 during enforcement.

instrument: Treaty of Ruby Valley, Oct. 1, 1863 (18 Stat. 689); ICC Docket 326-K; U.S. v. Dann, 470 U.S. 39 (1985)
basis: Treaty has no cession; Royce p. 828: 'No formal purchase... but the U. S. took possession'. ICC found title lost by 'gradual encroachment' (stipulated date July 1, 1872); Dann held the unaccepted $26M deposit was payment. CERD 2006 objected.

instrument: Treaty with the Shoshoni-Goship, Oct. 12, 1863 (13 Stat. 681)
basis: Royce: boundaries defined, U.S. took possession without formal purchase. ICC outcome not checked.

instrument: None (Tansey Point treaties of Aug. 1851 unratified)
basis: Royce records the country taken without any treaty; dataset types it executive_order. Lower Columbia part also covered by unratified Tansey Point treaties (reserved village, fishing and cranberry rights).

instrument: None
basis: Washo country recorded by Royce as taken without purchase or relinquishment; dataset legal_type is a link-based guess.

instrument: Fort Wise reserve, Feb. 18, 1861; ceded by Little Arkansas, Oct. 14, 1865 (14 Stat. 703)
basis: Promised reserve never furnished, partly leased to whites by agent Colley, occupied by troops; the Sand Creek massacre (Nov. 29, 1864) took place on or by it; ceded 11 months later by chiefs behind about 8 of 280+ lodges (Powell, via PSL p. 211). Little Arkansas Art. 6 reparations never paid (NPS).

instrument: Little Arkansas treaty, Oct. 18, 1865 (14 Stat. 717), reserve; superseded by the Medicine Lodge treaty, Oct. 21, 1867 (15 Stat. 581)
basis: Reservation reached by hostage-taking (Satanta and Lone Wolf, Dec. 1868). Post-1894 taking: Jerome count 456 of 562 per agent vs the Secretary's 1899 admission that fewer than three-fourths signed; Congress amended without resubmission; Lone Wolf (1903). Forgery alleged, never adjudicated. ICC Docket 32 net $2,067,166. 'Promised_reserved' is the 1894 snapshot; add a 1901 'taken_by_statute' overlay.
research_verification: confirmed (hostages, Art. 12, Lone Wolf, Docket 32); partly (counts, forgery)
revision_note: 2026-10-20: was promised_reserved. 478 is the 1865 Little Arkansas reserve, replaced by the smaller 1867 Medicine Lodge reservation; promised, then taken. The Jerome-agreement flags (consent threshold, Senate change, fraud) concern the 1867 reservation, which has no confirmed Royce polygon in the atlas, so they are no longer proposed here; the findings stay listed.

instrument: Medicine Lodge, Oct. 21, 1867 (15 Stat. 581); 1865 recognition (14 Stat. 717)
basis: ICC Dockets 257 and 259-A found recognized title under the 1865 treaty to about 39.68M acres (510, 511) and awarded $35.06M (1974); no land returned. Commission arrived with a predetermined removal plan (ICC Docket 257 record); Peace Commission act provided 4,000 volunteers if peace failed. Duress is asserted in PSL p. 41, scholarly-cited elsewhere.

instrument: Little Arkansas, Oct. 18, 1865 (14 Stat. 717) Art. 2; Medicine Lodge 1867
basis: 1865 reserve promised for 'absolute and undisturbed use' (with a presidential-designation escape clause) and cut back within two years; some Comanche bands absent, bound by accepting goods (Art. 6). Recognized title per ICC; $35.06M (1974).

instrument: Ute treaty, Mar. 2, 1868 (15 Stat. 619) Art. 1-3; earlier Conejos (Tabeguache) treaty, Oct. 7, 1863 (13 Stat. 673), which has no Royce polygon in the atlas
basis: The 1863 treaty was signed by Tabeguache leaders only but had them relinquish all land outside their reserve, including country of the Mouache, Capote, Weeminuche, Grand River and Yampa bands; those bands' relinquishment is 1868. Do not color Mouache, Capote or Weeminuche country 'ceded 1863'. Miners in South Park by 1859. 1868 Senate-amendment assents were taken band by band (confirmed).
research_verification: confirmed (1863 text, 1868 assents); partly (signer count, troops)

instrument: Fort Laramie treaty, Apr. 29, 1868 (15 Stat. 635)
basis: Royce p. 849 calls 516 a cession: "This cession comprises that portion of the Sioux territory assigned them by Fort Laramie treaty of 1851 within the present limits of South Dakota not included in the reservation described in the second article." It is not the Great Sioux Reservation (Art. 2), which is approximated by 598 + 699 + 700-705.

instrument: Recognized by Fort Laramie 1851; relinquished by Crow treaty May 7, 1868 (15 Stat. 649)
basis: Crow assent to the 1852 Senate amendment is disputed (Kappler footnote says all but the Crow assented; another text says Crow assented Sept. 18, 1854): flag applies only until resolved. Wind River basin assigned to the Crow in 1851 and the Shoshone in 1863 (Crowheart Butte).

instrument: Treaty of Bosque Redondo, June 1, 1868 (15 Stat. 667)
basis: Signed by Dine leaders while about 8,000-10,000 people were interned at Bosque Redondo, where up to about 3,500 died. Not flagged 'hostages': the population was interned, not held for a signature.

instrument: Fort Bridger, July 3, 1868 (15 Stat. 673) Art. 2; preceded by Fort Bridger, July 2, 1863 (18 Stat. 685) Art. 4
basis: 1863 recognized Shoshone country (Yampa and North Park in Colorado) and ceded nothing; the cession is 1868. Off-reservation hunting right survives (Herrera analog; Wooten 2023). Colorado boundary of 520 may differ from the Doty 1859 map by 40-50 miles (Robertson 2023, single source).

instrument: EO Aug. 10, 1869 reservation; Jerome agreement 1890, Act of Mar. 3, 1891
basis: Secretary Noble: get three-fourths 'but close with a majority if you cannot get more'; agent's 464-signature count not credible per Berthrong (about 680 needed); beef rations halved; attorneys' 10 percent contract ($67,000), bribery 'highly likely' (Hagan). Whether Medicine Lodge Art. 12 bound an EO reservation is itself arguable; the government acted as if it did. 1965 $15M settlement.

instrument: EO Apr. 12, 1870 (Fort Berthold); 1851 recognition; unratified Fort Berthold agreement, July 27, 1866
basis: Royce p. 787: 'the remainder of that tract being considered as ceded'. No cession instrument; crosswalk 'ceded' should be 'taken by executive order'.

instrument: None
basis: Royce p. 856: 'No treaty was ever made with these Indians... The U. S. simply took possession'. legal_type 'unknown' should be 'no_instrument'.

instrument: Lander/Brunot agreement, Sept. 26, 1872; Act of Dec. 15, 1874 (18 Stat. 291)
basis: Preamble admits mines and citizens' improvements already inside the 'absolute and undisturbed' reservation; 700,642 acres (299 U.S. 476); ICC Docket 63 (1954) found $27,500 'unconscionable' against $560,513.60 (PSL only). Fix USFS tribe name ('Sioux, Wahpeton' should be Shoshoni; override exists).

instrument: Fort Bridger, July 3, 1868 (15 Stat. 673) Art. 2; Shoshone Tribe v. U.S., 299 U.S. 476 (1937); 304 U.S. 111 (1938)
basis: Army settled the Northern Arapaho on the reservation in March 1878 over Shoshone protest; the Court held it a taking of an undivided half interest, compensated in money ($1,581,889.50 for the half interest). Post-1894: 1896 Hot Springs cession (amended by Congress, 1 sq mi to Wyoming), 1905 act (Wyoming v. EPA 2017 held diminished; Interior and EPA disagreed). Crosswalk 'unclear' should be 'reserved (as of 1894), half interest taken 1878'.

instrument: Brunot Agreement, Sept. 13, 1873; Act of Apr. 29, 1874 (18 Stat. 36)
basis: Miners trespassed from about 1870 and the U.S. did not remove them (1868 Art. 2); the Utes refused in 1872; Brunot then used a promise to recover Ouray's captive son (never kept) and wrote Ouray a $1,000 salary into the agreement while reporting 'no presents'. Ute understanding was a mountain-and-mines sale; hunting right kept in Art. 2. Southern bands, whose land made up most of the cession, said they were tricked (PSL only). ICC Docket 327 figures unresolved. 'hostages' not applied: the son was held by others, not by the U.S.

instrument: Brunot Agreement 1873 Art. I proviso; EO Aug. 17, 1876; Act of May 14, 1884 (23 Stat. 22, text not seen)
basis: Expressly reserved in 1873, drawn into the cession by survey, restored by EO 1876, returned to the public domain by the 1884 act; ICC excluded it from Docket 327 as 'not included in the cession'. Never ceded and not compensated in that docket.

instrument: EO Nov. 22, 1875 addition; EO Aug. 4, 1882 restoration; Confederated Bands of Ute v. U.S., 330 U.S. 169 (1947)
basis: Strip north of the true 1868 line added by EO after a survey placed the line 15-18 miles too far south; restored to public domain 1882. Supreme Court: Utes were 'tenants at the will of the Government' there, so no compensation (three justices dissented). Not 'judicially_found_taking': the Court held the opposite.

instrument: Agreement of Sept. 26, 1876; Act of Feb. 28, 1877 (19 Stat. 254); rider of Aug. 15, 1876 (19 Stat. 176, 192)
basis: Art. 16 'unceded Indian territory' given up under the 'sell or starve' rider with about 10 percent of adult men signing against the 1868 Art. 12 three-fourths rule. Northern Cheyenne marks added Sept. 28, 1877 by a minority (Bear Bow 1918). Sioux Nation's taking holding addressed the Black Hills; for 597 'taken' rests on the consent failure.

instrument: Act of Feb. 28, 1877 (19 Stat. 254); U.S. v. Sioux Nation, 448 U.S. 371 (1980)
basis: Supreme Court affirmed the 1877 act was a taking requiring just compensation (about $17.1-17.5M plus interest); the Sioux refuse the award. Crosswalk 'ceded' and legal_type 'statute' conflict; use taken_by_statute.

basis: Three-fourths consent reached only after commissioner Otto Mears paid Ute men $2 per signature (confirmed by several secondary sources; reimbursement by Kirkwood is single-source). Punitive act after Milk Creek applied to the Uncompahgre who took no part (1868 Art. 17); promised Grand/Gunnison reservation not delivered (ICC Docket 349, $300,000); 1881 removal under Mackenzie's 24-hour ultimatum. Royce: 'Sufficient signatures obtained', so 'consent_threshold_not_met' is not applied. Which of 616/617 is the ceded tract must be fixed first.
research_verification: confirmed (bribe, removal, Docket 349); partly (reimbursement, Royce number)
